Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes — started ~08:00 PDT after your canary

Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp p95/p99 latency regression for the Hosted API around 08:00 PDT. Error rates are low, but tail latency has increased by ~3x for long-context generation jobs (seq len ~2k). This began coincident with the model canary rollout noted in your status message.

Quick facts from our side:
- p50: ~120ms (unchanged)
- p95: 430ms -> 1.6s (observed rise at 08:07)
- p99: 900ms -> ~3.2s
- Throughput (rps): steady; we do not see traffic spikes on our end

We rely on tight tail latency for synchronous user flows — this is causing user-facing errors. Can you confirm whether the canary variant was rolled to production routing? If so, please advise mitigation steps and expected ETA for fix or rollback.

Attached: p95-chart.png (short window). Happy to join a call.

—Michael

Acme reports a p95/p99 tail latency spike coincident with the canary rollout we pushed this morning (model v2.3-alpha). They show steady throughput but significant tail degradation for long-context requests. Customer is high-touch and this is impacting revenue flows. Need immediate triage.

Subject: Re: INTERNAL: urgent — Acme p95/p99 regression after canary rollout (INF-2147)

Quick summary from on-call triage:
- Root cause (prelim): model variant v2.3-alpha introduced a small attention kernel change to optimize throughput. Under long sequence lengths (~1.5–2k tokens), the new kernel causes suboptimal memory access patterns on A100 nodes at particular batch sizes, increasing tail latency in ~10% of requests.
- Evidence: we see GC-like GPU memory stalls and serialized kernel invocations on the affected pods. p95 jump matches the timing of canary traffic.
- Canary traffic: yes — routing policy pushed ~15% traffic to v2.3-alpha (intended gradual canary).

Immediate mitigations we can enact in the next 20–30 minutes:
1) Reduce canary routing from ~15% -> 0% (route control change). This will remove new-orange variant from production flows.
2) Force routing of Acme's traffic to quantized v2.2.q4 which has demonstrated stable tail latency (no functional regression).
3) If rollback of v2.3-alpha is needed, we'll run a full revert deploy to restore previous kernel selection (timeline ~45–60m with safety checks).

Attachments: logs.tar.gz (preliminary GPU traces), p95-chart.png (compiled across customer requests).

I'll start the route control change now and follow with a deploy revert if we still see tail issues. Will post CLI commands and metrics snapshot to INF-2147.

—Dev
